method: Read-only inspection of the running vendor filesystem; copied the Keymaster service and modules to /private/tmp and inspected ELF dependencies/strings. No device files changed.

module_name_resolution.aosp_loader_behavior: hw_get_module_by_class first checks ro.hardware.<class>; then tries class.<variant>.so for ro.hardware, ro.product.board, ro.board.platform and ro.arch; finally it tries class.default.so.
module_name_resolution.candidate_msm8994_module: keystore.msm8994.so would not match the current property variants unless ro.hardware.keystore is set to msm8994 or the module is packaged under a matched variant name. No such module is currently installed. A class-specific property would avoid changing global ro.hardware or ro.board.platform, but property selection alone does not provide or validate a module.

keymaster_hidl_wrapper.embedded_fallback_message: Could not find any keystore module, using software-only implementation.

default_module_resolution.source_behavior: The default HIDL factory calls hw_get_module_by_class(KEYSTORE_HARDWARE_MODULE_ID, NULL, &mod). When no legacy keystore hardware module is found, it logs the software-only message and returns CreateKeymasterDevice() with no hardware device.

qualcomm_qsee_reference.legacy_module_behavior: The AOSP Qualcomm Keymaster HAL dynamically opens libQSEEComAPI.so, then calls QSEECom_start_app with /vendor/firmware/keymaster, app name keymaster, and an 8192-byte shared buffer.
qualcomm_qsee_reference.cityman_assets: The QSEEComAPI libraries exist, but the inspected mounted firmware has no keymaster/keymaster64 app directory, /dev/qseecom is absent, and the earlier FFU/runtime inventories found no separately named Keymaster trusted app.

interpretation: This identifies the immediate Android HAL fallback mechanism: the running default Keymaster 3.0 wrapper has no separate keystore hardware module to open and includes the AOSP software-only fallback. Cityman's module variants also do not select an msm8994-named file without an explicit keystore-specific override. QSEEComAPI libraries existing on disk are insufficient: no Keymaster trusted app is identified, the current device node is absent, and the generic Keymaster wrapper has no QSEEComAPI dependency. The prior QSEECOM-enabled temporary boot still produced SECURITY_LEVEL_SOFTWARE for a credential-bound key, so merely binding the QSEE driver is not a fix.
required_next_work: Find a matching, legally usable MSM8994 hardware keystore module and its required signed secure application from a compatible firmware/source set, then verify module selection, ABI, TrustZone version and trust-world signature compatibility.

If no compatible implementation and trusted app exist, a QSEE-backed Keymaster port would require the correct TEE interface, signed trusted application, provisioning and lifecycle integration; do not substitute a software key or report a software match as trusted.
Only after a genuine module is installed and selected, repeat credential-bound KeyInfo/attestation and HAT enforcement checks.
publication: local only; no commit, push, or PR
